level: Senior-to-staff IC, screened at the staff end of the band. Demonstrated scope is Owned/Led, not contributed — price at or near $340K and do not open with the floor.
rationale: AI-core archetype weights ai_evaluator near-decisive, and that seat lands on Strong AI fit with the candidate clearing the JD's three-part disambiguation test: weight-changing post-training (Tulu 3 first-author, RLHF Team Lead, Olmo co-lead, current GRPO work), trace-level judgment and metric scepticism (RewardBench, first-author, the JD's own grader language), with production research Python the one leg unconfirmed. No seat produced an evidenced disqualifier. The one genuine evidence-of-absence finding — never having optimised against a cost/latency/security/governance frontier for a paying customer — is real and ruled on, but it is an IS bullet and a ramp risk, not a non-negotiable and not in the disambiguation rule. The three findings that would block are all absence of evidence traceable to specific packet-capture failures: zero README or source content across all 26 repos (so craft is unscored for both the case and the rebuttal — open_source_dev conceded this honestly and senior_engineer holds the same bar), a stealth employer described in three lines, and a citation-sorted Scholar view that structurally buries the last two years. Confidence is low across every seat (44-64) and that is a verdict on the packet, not the man. Both seats that moved — open_source_dev from Strong talent to Solid, engineering_manager raising problem-match while holding Screen — cited new evidence, so neither is discounted. The only blocking verdict rests on a comp estimate, an inference from silence, and a characterisation the Fact Checker struck; it flips in either direction on a single question no one has yet put to him. A thirty-minute screen costs half an hour and resolves it; the alternative is never finding out whether the strongest open post-training record available was reachable.
rests_on: Weighed at reduced strength and named as required: (1) people_partner's beyond-stretch comp claim is BACKGROUND, a flagged estimate of what team-lead-titled profiles typically command, not a number he has stated; (2) people_partner's 'no stated growth path back to leading an org' is INFERENCE from silence in the role file, which describes no growth paths either way; (3) 'no-reports IC seat' was DOWNGRADED — the role file marks level and reports as inference, not ground truth; (4) ai_evaluator's TRL-as-production-research-Python was DOWNGRADED to inference (sixth-of-six co-authorship with no described contribution) and dgx-spark-setup struck as Shell, which is why the Python leg is unresolved rather than met; (5) science_lead was DOWNGRADED on the first-author count (three, not two — the 2019 quadrotor paper), though the correction does not disturb the independence read since Tulu 3 and RewardBench postdate the leadership titles; (6) science_lead's attribution of the GRPO post to the stealth org is inference from a headline plus a timestamp; (7) engineering_manager's environment-match finding is inference from a pattern across employer descriptions, well-grounded at the grain claimed but conceded to have overstated once (DeepMind internship omitted). The capability core — Tulu 3, RewardBench, OLMo family authorship, the titles — is untouched by any correction.
strongest_argument_against: The most evidenced finding in this sitting argues against me. Engineering_manager and science_lead reached it independently, from different lenses, and neither was corrected on the substance: across eight years and five employers with complete title-plus-description coverage, there is no instance of him optimising anything against an external constraint for anyone other than the open-research community. His own stated goal — 'the foundation of the open science of language models' — is close to the inverse of a JD whose success metric explicitly excludes publications. Stack on that a present-tense 'I'm starting a new research organization', a first research intern being credited last week, a 50K-subscriber business running in parallel for four years, and Congressional testimony, and people_partner's read is that this is a live, staffing-up founder for whom this seat is a title cut, a scope cut, and probably a pay cut. The sharp version: a recruiter screen is the worst possible instrument to detect motivation misalignment, because every candidate answers the mission question well, so the screen will return a false green and we will discover the regime-change problem four quarters in, having spent a staff-band offer and a headcount slot. I hold my decision anyway — the screen is thirty minutes and the questions below are answerable with facts rather than enthusiasm — but if the availability answer comes back 'live and funded', that argument wins and this should convert to a seat question, not a longer process.

open_questions.question: What base would he actually accept, and is the stealth organisation live-and-funded, live-and-unfunded, or paused? Ask for the number and the funding status as facts, not as comfort levels.
open_questions.what_the_answer_changes: A number above $340K plus a live, funded venture converts a background estimate into a packet fact and, with the already-factual title drop, hardens the over-qualification flag from soft to hard — at which point this stops being a candidate decision and becomes a seat decision (see route_note). A number inside the band plus a paused or shelved venture removes both the comp gap and the primary retention driver and returns this seat to Screen, leaving the other two flags standing independently.

open_questions.question: One artefact he personally authored end to end: a TRL commit or PR diff, a Tulu or OLMo post-training recipe script, or rlhf-book source. Read the code, not the star count.
open_questions.what_the_answer_changes: This is the third leg of the disambiguation rule and the only one not yet met. Production-grade research Python confirmed moves him from two-of-three (adjacent role, by the JD's own rule) to three-of-three (match). Source that turns out to be book-build tooling and nothing else, with no training-loop code anywhere he authored, is the one finding in this sitting that could still produce an evidenced NO_HIRE — which is precisely why it must be pulled rather than argued.

open_questions.question: Has he built or tuned a multi-step agentic system — tools, subagents, retrieval, validation loops — as opposed to single-turn post-training and reward modelling on static completions? Ask about the stealth org's work and about recent output the citation-sort buries.
open_questions.what_the_answer_changes: Yes moves him from strong on the model half to strong on both halves of the JD's mandate and makes this a straightforward hire at the top of the band. No leaves a real gap on the harness half, but one that sits outside the disambiguation triad and is learnable inside the 6-10 week ramp engineering_manager already estimated — it changes the offer's framing and the first-quarter plan, not the decision.

open_questions.question: Anywhere in his career, has he traded model quality against cost, latency, security or governance for a customer, a budget, or a compliance requirement — and separately, what does the stealth organisation actually build, for whom, and under what constraints?
open_questions.what_the_answer_changes: This is science_lead's question too; science_lead explicitly handed it to this seat. A single concrete instance converts my ruled evidence-of-absence into a capture gap and removes the largest non-comp risk. Nothing at all confirms the finding and means the hire is a genuine regime change — still hireable given the capability core, but it should be named openly in the offer conversation and built into the first-quarter scorecard rather than discovered later.

route_note: Run the recruiter call first and in this order: people_partner's number-and-venture-status question gates everything, because if he is unavailable at this band the code pull and the harness question cost effort for nothing. If the answer is band-acceptable and the venture is paused, proceed straight to senior_engineer's code pull and ai_evaluator's harness question in the same technical screen, with engineering_manager's constraint question folded into that conversation. If the answer is a number beyond $340K plus a live funded venture, do not reject the person — rule on the seat instead: the honest options are rescope_up to a staff-plus or founding-post-training seat with a band the hiring manager actually sets, or partner_or_advisor, which the JD itself gestures at when it names 'external research partners' among the hire's counterparties. A person building an open-models organisation is a more natural research partner to Harvey than an IC report, and that route is worth pricing before anyone writes a decline.
